title: Engineering Three-dimensional Epithelial Tissues Embedded within Extracellular Matrix
protocol: Prepare 100 ml solvent by adding 50 μl of concentrated HCl to 100 ml distilled water (dH2O).
Dilute the powdered insulin stock with prepared solvent to make a 5 mg/ml solution of insulin.
Dilute the 10x phosphate-buffered saline (PBS) stock solution to 1x with dH2O under sterile conditions.
Mix the PDMS prepolymer together with the curing agent in a 10:1 (w:w) ratio.
To 500 ml of stock Dulbecco's Modified Eagle Medium: Nutrient Mixture F-12 (DMEM/F-12), add 10 ml of sterile fetal bovine serum (FBS), 500 μl of gentamicin reagent, and 500 μl of 5 mg/ml insulin.
Add 1% (w:v) solution of BSA powder to 1x PBS and mix thoroughly.
Add 50 µl 10x Hank's balanced salt solution (HBSS) buffer, 30 µl 0.1 N sodium hydroxide (NaOH), 30 µl cell culture medium, and 400 µl of stock collagen to a chilled 1.5 ml microcentrifuge tube.
Mix slowly by pipetting up and down; avoid introducing bubbles.
Briefly centrifuge the mixture at 4 °C to remove any bubbles.
Dilute 16% paraformaldehyde 1:4 (v:v) in 1x PBS to prepare a fixative solution.
Dilute the stock nuclei labeling solution 1:1,000 (v:v) in 1x PBS.
Mix 1x PBS with 0.3% (v:v) detergent to prepare a 0.3% phosphate-buffered saline and detergent (PBST) solution.
Dilute goat serum 1:10 (v:v) in 0.3% PBST to prepare blocking buffer.
Dilute primary antibody (for example, rabbit anti-focal adhesion kinase (FAK)) 1:200 (v:v) in blocking buffer to prepare a primary antibody solution for a particular protein of interest.
Dilute fluorescent probe-conjugated secondary antibody (for example, goat anti-rabbit) 1:1,000 (v:v) in blocking buffer to prepare a secondary antibody solution.
Make a PDMS solution at the same ratio as described and mix thoroughly.
Place the mixture in a vacuum chamber for 15-30 min to remove any air bubbles introduced during mixing.
Pour the degassed solution into a plastic weigh boat or Petri dish containing a silicon master patterned with desired geometry features.
Cure the PDMS solution at 60 °C for ~12 hr.
Spin-coat an epoxy-based photoresist on top of a silicon wafer.
Expose the photoresist-coated wafer to UV light through a mask detailing desired stamp features.
Wash away soluble photoresist, leaving crosslinked photoresist in place to form desired features.
Cure PDMS around the imprinted features on the silicon master.
Separate PDMS from the silicon wafer using a clean razor blade.
Cut the PDMS patterned with imprinted features into individual rectangular stamps (~8-mm x 5-mm) with a razor blade.
Store feature-side-up rectangular stamps in a clean 100-mm-diameter Petri dish.
Spread ~2-3 g of PDMS solution evenly on a 100-mm-diameter Petri dish using a spin coater.
Cure the thin layer of PDMS for ~12 hr at 60 °C.
Cut the cured PDMS into rectangles (~5 mm x 2 mm) using a razor blade.
Immerse PDMS stamps and supports in 70% ethanol for sterilization.
Dry PDMS stamps and supports using an aspirator in a biosafety cabinet.
Add a drop of approximately 50 μl of 1% BSA in PBS to the top of each stamp.
Place BSA-covered stamps at 4°C for a minimum of 4 hours.
Aspirate BSA solution from the PDMS stamps.
Wash the surfaces of the stamps twice with cell culture medium.
Handle sterilized PDMS stamps and supports using curved stainless steel tweezers.
Lay out one 35-mm-diameter tissue culture dish for each PDMS stamp.
Place two PDMS supports in each dish separated by a distance slightly less than the length of the stamps.
Sterilize circular glass coverslips (15 mm in diameter, #1) using 70% ethanol.
Aspirate excess liquid from sterilized coverslips.
Store washed coverslips in a separate 100-mm-diameter Petri dish.
Dispense approximately 50 μl of the collagen mixture to evenly coat the surface of each PDMS stamp.
Pick up each collagen-coated PDMS stamp with tweezers.
Gently invert the stamps.
Lower the inverted stamps on top of the PDMS supports laid out in 35-mm-diameter tissue culture dishes such that the collagen is between the stamp and the bottom of the dish.
Incubate the dishes at 37 °C for 30 min.
Dispense ~50 µl of the remaining collagen mixture onto each of the circular coverslips.
Incubate the coverslips at 37 °C for 30 min.
Aspirate the cell culture medium from a tissue culture dish containing epithelial cells at ~40% confluency.
Wash once with 10 ml 1x PBS.
Add 2 ml of trypsin to the cells and incubate at 37 °C for 5-10 min.
Add 8 ml of fresh culture medium to the tissue culture dish containing trypsinized cells, detaching any remaining adherent cells from the dish.
Mix gently by pipetting and move the cell mixture to a 15 ml conical tube.
Centrifuge at 100 × g for 5 min.
Aspirate the supernatant from the conical tube.
Resuspend the cell pellet in cell culture medium.
Count the cells using a hemocytometer to determine concentration.
Adjust suspension volume to obtain a final concentration of ~10^6-10^7 cells/ml.
Remove gelled collagen samples from the incubator.
Gently lift PDMS stamps straight upwards with tweezers to detach them from the molded collagen.
Discard the PDMS stamps.
Dispense ~30 µl of concentrated cell suspension onto each collagen gel containing molded cavities.
Observe cells under a brightfield microscope with a 10X/0.25 NA objective.
Gently shake dishes side to side to promote cell settling within the cavities.
Check that the cavities are filled within ~5 min.
Tilt each tissue culture dish on its side.
Gently dispense ~400 μl of cell culture medium over the surface of the collagen gel.
Aspirate the liquid.
Repeat wash 1-2 more times.
Check the collagen gels under the microscope in between each wash.
Place the tissue culture dishes into a cell culture incubator at 37 °C for 15 min.
Gently invert the collagen-coated glass coverslips and place them on top of the cell-filled collagen molds such that the collagen forms a cap over the cavities.
Incubate the samples at 37 °C for 15 min to allow the collagen caps to adhere.
Dispense ~2-2.5 ml of cell culture medium slowly over the glass coverslip on top of the gels.
Culture the samples at 37 °C for 1-3 days.
Aspirate the cell culture medium from the tissue culture dishes.
Add enough fixative solution to cover the cell-containing gels and incubate at room temperature for 15 min on a shaker at 200 rpm.
Aspirate the fixative, fill the tissue culture dishes with 1x PBS, and incubate at room temperature for 15 min on a shaker at 200 rpm.
Repeat the PBS wash twice for three total washes.
Aspirate the PBS from the tissue culture dish and replace with Hoechst solution.
Incubate at room temperature for 15-20 min to label nuclei.
Aspirate the nuclear labeling solution.
Wash the cell-containing gels three times with 1x PBS.
Store stained samples in 1x PBS at 4°C until further use.
Aspirate the PBS from the tissue culture dishes.
Add 300 μl of 0.3% PBST to the samples and incubate for 15 min at room temperature.
Aspirate the 0.3% PBST, cover the gels with blocking buffer, and incubate on a shaker (200 rpm) at room temperature for ~4 hr.
Aspirate the blocking buffer, cover the gels with primary antibody solution, and incubate overnight at 4°C on a shaker at 200 rpm.
Aspirate the primary antibody solution, add 0.3% PBST solution, and incubate on a shaker at room temperature for 30 min.
Aspirate the 0.3% PBST and repeat every 30 min for 3-4 hr.
Repeat steps with secondary antibody solution.
Wrap tissue culture dishes with aluminum foil to prevent photobleaching of the secondary antibody.
After the final wash, store stained samples in 1x PBS at 4°C until further use.
Visualize samples using a 10X/0.30 NA objective focused on the midplane of epithelial tissues.
Image fixed samples labeled with a nuclear marker under UV illumination using a 10X/0.30 NA objective.
To visualize samples stained for a protein of interest, image using a 10X/0.30 NA objective on an inverted fluorescence microscope.
Import each tissue image using standard image analysis software.
Convert the imported images to 8-bit grayscale.
Threshold the grayscale images by converting them to binary.
Define a grayscale cutoff point for thresholding.
Values below the threshold become black, values above become white.
Combine individual binary images into a single image stack.
Register the stacked images in the analysis software.
Use each image as a template to align subsequent images.
Align all images in the stack using propagation alignment.
Overlay the aligned images based on average intensity.
Form a single image with a pixel frequency map.
Color-code the frequency map using image editing software.
